returnedSources.snippet: 初创公司使用 AI “码农” Devin 一个月的体验 号令天下。这种合作模式,和团队里带新人的方式,非常相似。 上手体验:流畅得不像AI Devin的使用体验和上手流程,设计得相当出色。只需将它连接到你的GitHub仓库,它就会自动分析你的代码库,了解主要组件、编译步骤、代码风格和最佳实践。即便对我们这样的初创公司来说,代码库内容不算丰富,Devin也能自动推理出构建流程的基本要素。 初步分析完成后,Devin会展示其结果,并邀请你根据每个源码目录的需要,补充额外的安装或配置步骤。为了验证配置是否正确,它还会尝试执行所有步骤。 指派新任务也很直接。目前它还没法对接Linear或Jira这类任务管理系统,就是一个简单的文本框,输入任务描述就行。(你也能在Slack的摘录对话串里标记任务,但实测下来,感觉效率不高。) (图片来源:Cognition的Devin。使用聊天界面是最快的指派任务方式。) 当你指派一个新任务时,Devin会先审查代码库来制定行动计划,确定它认为应该修改的代码。你能在web app里实时目睹它审查文件和修改代码的全过程(这个功能挺酷的)。完成后,它会运行代码检查和测试,解决问题,最后创建一个PR(pull request)。你可以在PR里留言,指导它修改或修复bug。 一句话总结:Devin的上手体验,直观且易于融入工程团队的工作流程。 强项:小范围、明确定义的代码修改 Devin最擅长的,是范围狭窄、定义明确的代码修改,这些修改只涉及单个组件和少数几个代码文件。我们最初让它完成的任务包括:优化饼图的显示格式、修正API返回数据时的边界问题、以及在创建新数据源时设定默认的更新计划。这些活儿如果由人来干,每个大概需要花一小时去研究、实施和测试。但有了Devin,只需一两分钟描述任务,再用五分钟检验它完成的工作,就能合并。 (图片来源:Cognition公...

returnedSources.title: One month of using Devin
returnedSources.snippet: Scott Wu (the CEO of Cognition) shared his team’s mental model for using Devin in an interview that we found quite interesting: The “right” way to use Devin is to give it a task first thing in the morning and let it run while you’re doing other work. A few hours later, you can come back to it, inspect the progress it made, and provide any necessary guidance. By the end of the day, it should have been able to complete the task you set it. This aligns very well with how you might collaborate with [...] Where Devin excels is in making narrowly-scoped and well-defined changes that are restricted to a single component and touch a few files. Some of the first things that we had it do were: improve the formatting of a pie chart, fix an edge case in how our API was returning data, and set a default update schedule when creating a new data source. Each of these tasks would have taken a person about an hour to investigate, implement, and test. With Devin, it took a minute or two to write a task [...] ### Introduction Devin presents itself as a fairly humble and self-aware tool. The expectation it sets is that it’s a junior software engineer that’s able to accomplish tasks with sufficiently specific guidance. Its rule of thumb is that ~3 hours of work can be accomplish autonomously before they worry about the agent diverging. The expectation setting was clear and quite helpful, and this aligns well with what we’ve written previously about AI work and human handoffs.

returnedSources.title: Devin AI Review: My Experience Testing It as a Non-Coder | Lindy
returnedSources.snippet: No, Devin cannot replace a software engineer. It can automate scoped coding work, but still needs human oversight for creative and complex problems. ### What is Devin Cognition? Devin Cognition, also called Devin by Cognition, is an AI coding tool that lets engineering teams automate tasks like debugging, planning, and refactoring. ### What’s the best Devin AI alternative? [...] Devin AI is worth it for teams that manage a consistent number of engineering tasks every month. These teams can reduce handoffs and save developer time by using Devin to run planning, coding, and testing in one environment. [...] Devin will work for you if you need an AI coding agent that can execute well-defined tasks, like planning and pull requests. It handles bug fixes, refactors, and prototypes with autonomy, and is more capable than autocomplete tools. However, you must understand its trade-offs like unpredictable costs and limited creative problem-solving. Devin works for scoped engineering work, but it isn’t designed to replace human engineers.

returnedSources.title: Devin, the AI Engineer: Review, Testing & Limitations in 2026 | Idlen
returnedSources.snippet: This is an honest, in-depth review based on extensive testing across real-world projects. No sponsored content, no affiliate links—just a thorough assessment of what Devin can and cannot do in 2026. ## What Is Devin? ### Overview Devin is an autonomous AI software engineer built by Cognition Labs. Unlike copilots that assist you while you code, Devin takes a task description and works independently—planning, coding, testing, debugging, and iterating until the task is complete. [...] We tested Devin across a range of tasks on real codebases to evaluate its capabilities honestly. Here are the results. ### Test Setup Codebases: 5 real-world projects (React/Next.js frontend, Node.js API, Python data pipeline, Django web app, Go microservice) Task types: Bug fixes, feature additions, refactoring, test writing, documentation Evaluation criteria: Correctness, code quality, time to completion, number of interventions needed ### Test Results Summary [...] ## Conclusion Devin is a genuinely impressive piece of technology that delivers real value when used correctly. It is not the "replacement for software engineers" that some headlines suggested, but it is a powerful tool that can handle a significant portion of well-defined engineering tasks autonomously.

returnedSources.title: Devin's 2025 Performance Review: Learnings From 18 Months of Agents At Work | Cognition
returnedSources.snippet: A few standout examples: One large organization saved 5-10% of total developer time by using Devin for security fixes. Another saw 20x efficiency gain: human developers average 30 minutes per vulnerability, Devin, 1.5 minutes. ### Language and framework upgrades, migrations, and modernization Customers use Devin for modernization and migrations, like SAS → PySpark, COBOL, Angular → React, .NET Framework → .NET Core, or switching off proprietary frameworks. [...] Once it gets instructions on how to update each repo, a fleet of Devins can execute on every repo in parallel. This results in massive savings. A few examples from this year: A large bank was migrating hundreds of thousands of proprietary ETL framework files. Devin completed each file's migration in 3-4 hours vs 30-40 for human engineers (10x improvement). When Oracle sunsetted legacy support for one Java version, Devin was able to migrate each repo in 14x less time than a human engineer. [...] ### Scope changes and iterative collaboration Devin handles clear upfront scoping well, but not mid-task requirement changes. It usually performs worse when you keep telling it more after it starts the task. This differs from human juniors: you can coach a human through iterative problem-solving. This puts more of a responsibility on the engineer to scope work well up-front. Engineers working with Devin have to adjust to learning how to "manage" Devin effectively.

returnedSources.title: Introducing Devin - Devin Docs
returnedSources.snippet: Devin is an autonomous AI software engineer that can write, run and test code. Devin can handle most tasks, excluding extremely difficult tasks. As a rule of thumb, if you can do it in three hours, Devin can most likely do it. Ask Devin to tackle Linear/Jira tickets, implement entirely new features, repro and fix bugs, build internal tools, and more! See what’s new with Devin in our release notes! [...] 1. Tackling many tasks in parallel, before they end up in your backlog Linear/Jira tickets Entire features from scratch Bug reports App testing 2. Code migrations, refactors, and modernization Language migrations (e.g. JavaScript to TypeScript) Framework upgrades (e.g. Angular 16 -> 18) Monorepo to submodule conversions Removing unused feature flags Extracting common code into libraries 3. Common, repetitive engineering tasks PR Review Codebase Q&A [...] To get the best results from Devin: Write clear prompts with explicit completion criteria — the clearer the task, the higher the success rate, especially for complex work. Make tasks easy to verify — e.g. checking that CI passes or testing an automatic deployment. For harder tasks, break them into well-scoped steps and provide relevant context or examples. citationChecks.reason: 原句为Hacker News评论者直接质问“Devin似乎并未完成所要求的任务，即提供AWS使用说明吗？”，是评论者本人对演示的看法，并未自称转述他人；但该评论针对的演示（Cognition官方Twitter发布的Upwork演示）由原文位置与检索时间/标题间接关联。原句确实支持‘Devin似乎未完成所要求任务（提供AWS使用说明）’这一说法，并明确将其归属为Hacker News评论。摘要附加的‘转述’和具体日期2024年3月官方Twitter演示等细节在原句中并不直接可见，但评论发布于2024-03-13，标题为“Devin: AI Software Engineer”，与所指演示大体对应。原句本身并未声明未独立复现，但该声明属于来源标注而非事实主张；核心事实（评论者认为Devin似乎未完成AWS说明任务）由原句直接支持。

原句明确说‘Devin是我听说过的第一个AI开发工具——事实上也是我第一个使用的，因为我在私有测试阶段收到了邀请。现在这个产品似乎已经在cursor等其他工具之间褪色（变得无关紧要？）’。这支持‘第一个听说/第一个使用（私有测试受邀）’及‘似乎已被其他工具边缘化’的个人经历与观感；作者为edude03，发布于2026-09-08，与适用范围一致。摘要中的‘未独立复现’属于来源标注，不影响核心事实。

answers.body:
来源报告（未独立复现）：Hacker News 有评论者转述，在 2024 年 3 月讨论的 Upwork 演示中，Devin 似乎并未完成所要求的任务（提供 AWS 使用说明）。
适用范围：Hacker News 评论；针对 2024 年 3 月官方 Twitter 上发布的 Upwork 演示 [1]

来源报告（未独立复现）：Hacker News 有评论者称 Devin 是其听说过的第一个 AI 开发工具，也是其在私有测试阶段受邀使用的第一个此类工具，并认为该产品如今似乎已被其他工具边缘化。
适用范围：Hacker News 评论者 edude03 的个人经历与观感；2026 年 9 月发帖 [2]

尚不能确定：Cognition 官方博客标题将 Devin 称为“首个 AI 软件工程师”。
保存原句为“first AI software engineer”，不等于“首个自主软件工程师”；摘录亦未含“自主”“独立完成”表述。（条件：cognition.com 官方博客标题；未标注日期与版本）

尚不能确定：来源报告（未独立复现）：一名开发者在 dev.to 上报告称，其在两周内用 10 个真实待办任务测试 Devin，结果完成了 3 个。
原句仅称花两周给 Devin 真实任务，标题含“10 个完成 3 个”，正文摘录未述完成数，未能由原句直接核实。（条件：dev.to 个人博客；未标注产品版本、套餐与日期）

核查缺口：
• 已读官方博客摘录仅含“first AI software engineer”，未保存“自主”“独立完成软件工程任务”的原句，无法核实该复合表述。
• dev.to 正文摘录未包含“10 个任务完成 3 个”的原句，完成数仅见于标题，缺少正文依据。
